sub: Named after the Prophet Nūḥ, whose story fills the whole surah
theme: Nūḥ’s long call to his people, their stubborn refusal, and their end in the Flood. It shows the Makkans that treating the Prophet ﷺ the same way leads to the same end.
story: One of the early surahs revealed in Makkah, at a time when opposition to the Prophet ﷺ had grown strong and active.

It tells only one story, Nūḥ’s, because he stayed among his people so long, 950 years, calling them again and again to worship Allah alone. Most of it is his own report to his Lord of everything he tried.
The message to Makkah is never said outright, but it is clear: you are treating Muhammad ﷺ the way Nūḥ’s people treated Nūḥ. If you don’t change, you will meet their end.

sections.title: Warn your people before it comes
sections.meaning: Allah sent Nūḥ with one task: warn his people before a painful punishment arrives. He tells them plainly: worship Allah, fear Him and obey me. Then Allah will forgive your sins and let you live out your term. But when Allah’s set time comes, it cannot be pushed back.
points: Nūḥ sent: warn your people before a painful punishment
“I am a clear warner: worship Allah, fear Him, obey me”
He’ll forgive you and give you time; His deadline won’t be delayed
sections.matters: In three words, worship, taqwā and obedience, it gives the message of every prophet: worship Allah alone, fear Him, and follow His messenger. It also sets the stakes: a window of time, and a deadline that will not move.
sections.story: No specific incident. It opens Nūḥ’s story, told to the people of Makkah as a warning.
explained: Allah sent Nūḥ to his people out of mercy, to warn them of a painful punishment, in this world and the next, if they kept on disbelieving. Nūḥ said: “I am a clear warner.” He made plain what to fear and how to be saved, and summed it up: worship Allah, fear Him, obey me.

If you do, Allah will forgive your sins and let you live out your lifespan without punishment. But no life lasts forever, and when Allah’s set time comes, it cannot be delayed. If only you knew, you would believe before it is too late.
teaches: Every prophet’s message: worship Allah, fear Him, follow His messenger.
Warning people is an act of mercy.
Turning to Allah brings forgiveness and time.
Act before your appointed time comes; it won’t be moved.
sections.hook: Andhir, “warn” (1), is answered by nadhīr, “warner” (2). Ayah 4 uses two words twice: yuʾakhkhirkum ilā ajal, “He delays you to a term”, then ajal Allāh… lā yuʾakhkhar, “Allah’s term is not delayed”.

sections.title: Night and day, openly and in secret
sections.meaning: Nūḥ reports to his Lord: he called his people night and day, and they only ran further, blocking their ears and covering their heads. He called publicly and privately. He promised that seeking forgiveness brings rain, wealth, children, gardens and rivers, and pointed to their own creation, the heavens, the sun, moon and earth.
points: Called night and day; they fled, fingers in ears, heads covered
Called openly, announced publicly, and spoke in private
Seek forgiveness: rain, wealth, children, gardens, rivers
Why no awe of Allah, who made you in stages?
Seven heavens in layers; the moon a light, the sun a lamp
Grown from the earth, returned to it, brought out again
The earth spread out for you, with wide roads
sections.matters: It is a model for calling people to Allah: at every hour, in every way, with hope and with warning, using proofs from their own lives and the sky above them. The more Nūḥ gave, the more they ran, and still he kept going.
sections.story: No specific incident. Ayat 10–12 are tied to praying for rain: when ʿUmar went out to pray for rain, he only sought forgiveness and recited these ayat, saying he had asked for rain with the keys of the sky.
explained: After centuries, Nūḥ reports to his Lord. He called his people night and day, and they only ran further. Whenever he called them to be forgiven, they pushed fingers into their ears and pulled clothes over their heads so they wouldn’t hear or see him. So he called loudly in public, and spoke to them privately, one by one.

His message was full of hope: ask your Lord’s forgiveness, for He forgives again and again. He will send steady rain and give you wealth, children, gardens and rivers. Then came a question: why don’t you hold Allah in awe?

Then the proofs. He made you stage by stage. He built seven heavens in layers and set the moon in them as a light and the sun as a lamp. He grew you from the earth, will return you to it and bring you out again, and spread it out for you to travel its wide roads.
teaches: Keep calling to good: day and night, in public and in private.
Istighfār brings rain, wealth and children, not only forgiveness.
Your own growth, stage by stage, points to your Creator.
The One who grew you from the earth can bring you out of it again.
Mix hope with warning when you call people to Allah.
sections.hook: Daʿawtu, “I called”, returns at 5, 7 and 8. Ayat 5–14 all end in -ārā: nahārā, firārā, istikbārā, jihārā … aṭwārā. At 15, where the heavens begin, the rhyme changes: ṭibāqā, sirājā.

sections.title: The chiefs’ plot and five idols
sections.meaning: Nūḥ tells his Lord: they disobeyed me and followed chiefs whose wealth and children only added to their loss. Those chiefs plotted hugely and told the people: never abandon your gods, Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq and Nasr. They have misled many, so Nūḥ prays that the wrongdoers gain nothing but more straying.
points: They disobeyed me and followed those whose wealth only brought loss
“Never leave your gods: Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq, Nasr”
They misled many; increase the wrongdoers only in error
sections.matters: It shows how false worship takes hold and stays: ordinary people follow the powerful, and the powerful defend the old idols. It also traces idol worship to its start, honouring righteous men with statues until later generations worshipped them.
sections.story: No specific incident. The five names belonged to righteous men of long ago. After they died, statues were set up to remember them; once that generation passed and knowledge faded, the statues were worshipped. The same idols later turned up among Arab tribes.
explained: Nūḥ’s message did nothing for them. The ordinary people followed their chiefs, men blessed with wealth and children that only led them deeper into loss. Those chiefs plotted a huge plot: they rejected Nūḥ, harmed him and his followers, and convinced the people they were on the truth.

They said: never abandon your gods, the ways of your forefathers, and they named them: Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq and Nasr. Many were misled. Then Nūḥ prayed that the wrongdoers gain nothing but error. This was not impatience: Allah had told him that no one else from his people would believe.
teaches: Don’t follow people just because they have wealth and status.
Honouring righteous people too much was the first step to idol worship.
Wealth and children can add up to nothing but loss.
Leading others astray multiplies the harm.
sections.hook: The five names in 23: lā before Wadd, Suwāʿ and Yaghūth, then only wa before Yaʿūq and Nasr. Ayah 21 ends illā khasārā; ayah 24 ends illā ḍalālā.

sections.title: Drowned, and Nūḥ’s final prayer
sections.meaning: For their sins they were drowned, then put into a Fire, with no one to help them against Allah. Nūḥ had prayed: leave not one disbeliever on earth, for they would mislead Your servants and raise only disbelievers. He ends asking forgiveness for himself, his parents, every believer in his house, and all believers.
points: Drowned for their sins, then into a Fire, with no helpers
Leave no disbeliever on earth; they’d mislead others and raise only disbelievers
Forgive me, my parents, believers in my house, all believers
sections.matters: The outcome of centuries of warning comes in a single ayah: drowned, then Fire. And Nūḥ’s last words are a prayer for all believers, living and dead, until the end of time, a prayer we can make our own.
sections.story: No specific incident. Nūḥ prayed against his people only after Allah told him no more of them would believe (11:36). Allah answered: every disbeliever drowned, even his own son, and the believers in the ship were saved.
explained: Min khaṭīʾātihim: because of their sins, above all disbelief and idol worship, they were drowned in the Flood and then entered into a Fire: either right after drowning, in the life of the grave, or in the Hereafter. No one besides Allah could help them.

Nūḥ had prayed: “Leave not a single disbeliever living on the earth.” After 950 years among them, and with Allah telling him none would believe, he knew they would only mislead others. Reportedly a father would bring his son to Nūḥ and say: “Beware of this liar; my father warned me about him.”
His final prayer is mercy: forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and all believing men and women. And give the wrongdoers nothing but ruin.
teaches: Sin has consequences, in this world and the next.
No one can protect you from Allah except His own mercy.
Pray for your parents, your household and all believers.
Begin your duʿāʾ with yourself, then widen it to others.
sections.hook: Nūḥ’s last two prayers open with rabbi: rabbi lā tadhar (26), rabbi ighfir lī (28). The surah ends illā tabārā, echoing illā firārā (6), illā khasārā (21) and illā ḍalālā (24).

groups.text: Allah sent Nūḥ to warn his people before a painful punishment, and he told them: I am a clear warner.
Worship Allah, fear Him and obey me; He will forgive you and give you time, but His deadline won’t move.
Nūḥ called them night and day, and they ran: blocking their ears, covering their heads, growing proud.
He called them openly, announced it publicly, and spoke to them in private.
Seek forgiveness, and Allah will send rain and give you wealth, children, gardens and rivers.
Why don’t you hold Allah in awe, when He created you stage by stage?
Allah made seven heavens in layers, with the moon a light in them and the sun a lamp.
He grew you from the earth, will return you to it, and will bring you out again.
He spread the earth out for you so you can travel its wide roads.
They disobeyed Nūḥ, followed chiefs whose wealth only brought loss, and plotted a huge plot.
The chiefs said: never leave your gods, Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq and Nasr. They misled many.
Drowned for their sins, then put into a Fire, they found no one to help them against Allah.
Nūḥ prayed: leave no disbeliever on earth, or they will mislead Your servants and raise only disbelievers.
Forgive me, my parents, the believers in my house and all believers; give the wrongdoers only ruin.

1.explain: Allah sent Nūḥ to his people out of mercy, to warn them of a painful punishment, in this world and the next, if they refused to believe.

2.explain: Nadhīrun mubīn: a clear warner. He made plain what they should fear, what to avoid and how to be saved, in a language they understood.

3.explain: The whole message in three commands: worship Allah alone, have taqwā of Him by avoiding what He forbids, and obey me in what I tell you.

4.explain: Min dhunūbikum: either all your sins, or your past sins, while wrongs done to people still need putting right. He lets you live out your term unpunished, but Allah’s set time won’t be delayed.

5.explain: Rabbi: Nūḥ turns to Allah with his report. He called his people night and day without stopping, for 950 years, obeying Allah’s command.

6.explain: Firārā: running away. The more he called them to the truth, the more they fled from it and turned their backs.

7.explain: Every time he called them to be forgiven, they put fingers in their ears and pulled their clothes over their heads so they wouldn’t hear or see him. They persisted and grew arrogant.

8.explain: Jihārā: then he called them openly, loudly, in front of everyone.

9.explain: He announced it in public, and he spoke to them in secret, one person at a time. He tried every door that might open.

10.explain: Istaghfirū: ask your Lord’s forgiveness and leave what you are doing. Ghaffār: He forgives again and again, any sin, even shirk, for whoever repents.

11.explain: Midrārā: rain, shower after shower, reviving the land. Rain had reportedly been held back from them. This is why these ayat are recited when praying for rain.

12.explain: He will increase your wealth and children and give you gardens and flowing rivers: the best of this world, for those who repent.

13.explain: Waqār: greatness. Why don’t you hold Allah in awe as He deserves, and fear Him? Or: why don’t you hope Allah will honour you if you believe?

14.explain: Aṭwārā: in stages. A drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh; then infancy, childhood and youth. The One who made you once can bring you back.

15.explain: Look how Allah created seven heavens ṭibāqā, in layers, one above another. Something so vast points to its Creator.

16.explain: He made the moon a nūr, a light, and the sun a sirāj, a blazing lamp, brighter than the moon. Through them we tell nights, days, months and years.

17.explain: Anbatakum min al-arḍi nabātā: He grew you from the earth like plants, when He created your father Ādam from it.

18.explain: Then He returns you into it when you die, and brings you out of it again on the Day of Resurrection.

19.explain: Bisāṭā: the earth spread out like a carpet, level and ready for you to live on, farm and build.

20.explain: So that you can travel its subulan fijājā, its wide paths, wherever you want. Here Nūḥ’s speech to his people ends.

21.explain: Nūḥ says: they disobeyed me and followed their chiefs, whose wealth and children only increased them in khasār, loss: straying in this world and punishment in the next.

22.explain: Makran kubbārā: a huge plot. They denied Nūḥ, harmed him and his followers, and fooled their people into thinking they were right; in one report, they urged them to kill him.

23.explain: They told the people: never abandon your gods, never Wadd, Suwāʿ, Yaghūth, Yaʿūq or Nasr. These were names of righteous men whose statues were later worshipped.

24.explain: Through these idols the chiefs misled many. Nūḥ prays: give the wrongdoers nothing but more error. He prayed this after Allah told him no more of his people would believe.

25.explain: Because of their sins they were drowned, then entered into a Fire: either right after drowning, in the grave, or in the Hereafter. They found no one to help them against Allah.

26.explain: Dayyār: anyone living anywhere. “Leave not one disbeliever on the earth.” Allah answered: every disbeliever drowned, even Nūḥ’s own son.

27.explain: If You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and raise only wicked disbelievers. He knew this after 950 years among them, and Allah had told him.

28.explain: Forgive me, my parents (both believers), whoever enters my house as a believer (my home, my place of prayer, or my ship), and all believing men and women. Tabārā: ruin.
